title: The Harbor of Bellbird Bay
premise: Zephyrine Quintana built her career on other people's happily-ever-afters while quietly dismantling her own capacity for one, ever since the winter she and her college best friend-turned-rival, wedding photographer Ivo Marchetti, betrayed each other to survive a scandal that ended both their careers. A decade later, a destination wedding at Bellbird Bay traps them together when a snowstorm closes the coastal road, forcing them to co-plan the event of the bride—who turns out to be the woman whose wedding they once destroyed. As old wounds reopen, Zephyrine must choose between protecting her invisibility and claiming the love and identity she buried; they reconcile with their past selves, confess the truth to the bride, and end by building something new together—a small studio in the harbor town where Zephyrine finally attends a wedding as a guest, not a ghost.
about_author: Casper Halloran is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent seven years watching love from behind banquet tables before turning to fiction. They write from a rented cottage on the Atlantic coast, where the weather does most of the plotting.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She runs her Manhattan planning firm with surgical detachment, rehearsing her pitch for the Delacroix wedding at Bellbird Bay while dodging her sister's pleas to come home for the holidays. The emotional beat: control as armor, and the first crack—she can't remember the last time she cried.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Contract
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He arrives at Bellbird Bay Inn to shoot the wedding and discovers the planner is Zephyrine—the woman who testified against him ten years ago. Neither will withdraw; the bride, Camille Delacroix, refuses to hear why. The beat: cold professionalism stretched over live wires.

chapters.title: What the Storm Took
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The snowstorm hits early; the road closes, the ferry stops, and half the vendors cancel. Forced into the inn's back office with Ivo, they divide labor like soldiers negotiating a truce. The beat: proximity without permission, resentment sharpened by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A power outage and a bottle of contraband champagne loosen the decade-old silence; they relive the night everything broke—the forged contract, the accusation, the choice each made to save themselves. The beat: grief disguised as banter, ending with a kiss neither will acknowledge.

chapters.title: Camille Knows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Camille privately reveals she chose them deliberately: she was the jilted bride from the scandal, and she wants the truth before her vows. She gives them until the wedding to tell her everything—or she tells the guests herself. The beat: the past acquires a deadline.

chapters.title: Salt and Forgiveness, Unsold
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She walks the frozen harbor with the innkeeper Marisol, who lost her own family to an unsaid truth, and begins drafting a confession she can't finish. Meanwhile Ivo covers for her mistakes with a client, unprompted. The beat: the heart as trainable muscle beginning to retrain itself.

chapters.title: Rehearsal of Ruins
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The rehearsal dinner nearly collapses when a guest recognizes Ivo from the scandal coverage; Zephyrine publicly defends him, then privately accuses him of letting her do it. Their fight finally names what each sacrificed—and what each actually wanted. The beat: honesty as detonation.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the eve of the wedding, she visits the burned-out boathouse where the betrayal happened and writes two letters: one to Camille confessing all, one to her twenty-four-year-old self granting pardon. Ivo finds her there and adds his own confession. The beat: forgiveness begins inward, together.

chapters.title: Vows Before Vows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the ceremony, before the processional, they tell Camille the whole truth in the snow-covered garden. Her verdict—grief, then grace—redefines the day; she asks them to stand at her wedding anyway, not as staff but as witnesses. The beat: climax and absolution entwined.

chapters.title: A Guest at Last
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue in spring. The Harbor Studio opens above Marisol's chandlery; Zephyrine plans one wedding a season, no more, and sits in the pews for the first time in her life. Ivo's hand finds hers during the recessional. The beat: visibility chosen, family found, the muscle at rest.
